newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Jan leading index seen at 33.3.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Jan leading index seen at 33.3.

text.p: Japan's diffusion index of leading economic indicators for January is expected to fall below the so-called boom or bust mark of 50 for the first time in five months, according to economic institutions.
Most institutions expect the leading index to stand at 33.3 out of a possible 100, with one forecasting 44.4.
A figure of below 50 is generally taken as suggesting the economy will contract in the coming months. The index was 70.0 in December.
For the coincident index, which measures current economic conditions, the institutions expect a figure of 90.0, unchanged from December.
The Economic Planning Agency (EPA) is due to announce the data on Monday.
Economists said a fall below the 50 mark in the diffusion index of leading economic indicators may be temporary, and the index is likely to rise above 50 in February.

The economic indicators used for the index include machinery orders, floor space of housing starts and money supply. The EPA compares the indicators with those from three months earlier to calculate the index.

"Floor space of new houses was unusually high because housing investment was brisk three months ago as contracts made before October were not subject to a planned rise in Japan's consumption tax on April 1," said Yoshihiro Ishimaru, an economist at Daiwa Bank Research Institute.
